question: Why do many men often spread STIs without even knowing they have them?

options.A: Male anatomy completely blocks bacterial growth
options.B: Common pathogens only survive inside female tissues
options.C: Many infected men show no early symptoms at all
options.D: Routine blood tests always cure the infection early

explanation: It's tricky! Many guys feel completely healthy and normal while carrying an infection, which is why education and screening are so important. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h1)

question: How should you as a nurse talk to a male patient about his sexual health during an assessment?

options.A: By waiting until physical symptoms become severe
options.B: With strict suspicion of high-risk behaviors
options.C: With an open and non-judgmental attitude
options.D: By asking only married men about their partners

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from judgment, they are much more honest about their history. That helps us give them the best care possible! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which of these common infections is caused by a bacterium?
explanation: Chlamydia is a bacterial infection. Remember: bacterial bugs can be knocked out with the right antibiotics! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the big difference in how our bodies handle bacterial STIs compared to viral STIs?

options.A: Viral infections only affect the skin, while bacteria only affect internal organs
options.B: Viral infections respond quickly to standard doses of penicillin
options.C: Bacterial pathogens cause visible lesions, while viruses never show any external signs
options.D: Bacterial infections are cleared with antibiotics, whereas viral infections stay in the body long-term

explanation: Antibiotics wipe out bacteria completely, but viruses like HIV or herpes stick around in the body. Great to keep this distinction in mind for your exams! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h2)

question: How are most common male STIs primarily passed from person to person?

options.A: Inhaling airborne droplets from a coughing carrier
options.B: Swimming in public pools with contaminated water
options.C: Direct mucous membrane contact during sexual intercourse
options.D: Sharing eating utensils with an infected person

explanation: Most STIs need skin-to-skin or mucosal contact during sex to spread. They don't jump through pool water or shared spoons! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why do STI infections in the male urethra often lead to swelling and pus?

options.A: The body produces extra oil to protect the skin from dryness
options.B: White blood cells rush to the invasion site to fight the microbes
options.C: Urine mixes with blood cells to create a protective barrier
options.D: Microbes block normal urine flow and cause back pressure

explanation: Think of white blood cells as your body's emergency responders. When germs attack, they flood the area to fight back, creating that pus we see in infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the nursing term for pain or burning when a patient passes urine?
explanation: Dysuria is a classic clinical term worth memorizing. 'Dys-' means painful or difficult, and '-uria' refers to urine! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h4)

question: A male patient comes to the clinic with a thick yellow discharge from his urethra and burning pain when urinating. What is the most likely culprit?
explanation: That classic yellow discharge combined with burning urination is a textbook sign of Gonorrhea affecting the urethra. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which lab test is most commonly used to find Chlamydia and Gonorrhea in men quickly and accurately?
explanation: NAAT is the gold standard! It's super sensitive and can even be done using a simple urine sample. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why do doctors still order lab tests even when a male patient's physical symptoms look obvious?

options.A: Hospitals require blood tests for insurance billing purposes
options.B: Different STIs can present with very similar clinical signs
options.C: Antibiotics will not work without a written laboratory report
options.D: Physical exams cannot detect any form of genital infection

explanation: Many STIs look identical on the outside (like causing the same discharge or sores). Lab tests tell us the exact germ so we use the right drug. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is your main health-education priority when handing a patient his prescription for a bacterial STI?

options.A: Tell the patient to share excess pills with sexual partners
options.B: Instruct the patient to double the dose if a single pill is missed
options.C: Advise stopping the drugs immediately once discharge clears up
options.D: Emphasize finishing the entire medication course even if symptoms stop

explanation: Always remind patients: just because you feel better doesn't mean the bacteria are gone. Stopping early causes stubborn, drug-resistant infections! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h6)

question: How do antiviral medications help male patients who have genital herpes?

options.A: They permanently block all future sexual transmission risks
options.B: They completely eliminate the virus from nerve cells
options.C: They shorten outbreak duration and reduce symptom severity
options.D: They prevent the patient from ever contracting bacterial infections

explanation: Antivirals are great for calming down outbreaks and easing pain, but remember—they manage the virus; they don't cure it completely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h6)

question: What long-term problem can happen to the urinary tract from severe scarring due to untreated infections?
explanation: When the urethra gets badly inflamed and heals with scar tissue, it narrows down (a stricture), making it tough to pee normally. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h7)

question: How can an untreated STI eventually lead to male infertility?

options.A: By altering the chemical composition of saliva and sweat glands
options.B: By causing permanent erectile dysfunction within the first week
options.C: By causing chronic inflammation that damages sperm production and transport structures
options.D: By completely stopping the production of testosterone in the pituitary gland

explanation: If an infection travels up into delicate reproductive tubes like the epididymis, the resulting scars can block sperm pathways. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for tracking down and treating the sexual partners of an infected patient?

options.A: To collect financial fines for public health registries
options.B: To prevent immediate reinfection of the original patient
options.C: To test the partners for unrelated chronic diseases
options.D: To ensure the partners report to police authorities

explanation: Partner treatment breaks the ping-pong cycle! If you treat just one person, they'll likely catch it right back from their untreated partner. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended way to reduce the spread of STIs in men?

options.A: Stopping all antibiotic use to boost natural immunity
options.B: Participating in routine periodic screening tests
options.C: Ensuring prompt treatment of all identified sexual partners
options.D: Consistent and correct use of latex barrier condoms

explanation: Stopping antibiotics is a huge no-no! It leads to treatment failure and superbugs, not immunity. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h8)
